To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new SSFID topology can be used in power electronics based medium voltage distribution systems, the topology can be implemented with existing technology, and the proposed topology can be tested using the proposed Power Hardware-in-the-loop setup.
the proposed topology of the SSFIDs can be used in a wide variety of power electronics based distribution networks.
the design of a high-frequency Solid State Transformer (HF-SST) is presented.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new fault isolation technology for the FREEDM system.
developing the enabling technologies for the next-generation power electronics based distribution grid.
the development of a solid state isolation device for implementation on a power electronics based distribution network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SSFID design and implementation in the FREEDM system is feasible.
a solid-state fault isolation device is a viable option for implementation in power electronic based systems.
the proposed design is a promising candidate for the future power electronics based distribution grid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the SSFIDs are a key enabling technology for the power electronics based FREEDM system and that the proposed SSFIDs are capable of handling high fault current levels with low on-state losses, low material costs, and low on-state losses.
a SSFID is needed to protect power electronic based distribution system from fault currents.
the design of a solid state circuit breaker is possible, but the material cost and the on-state loss are still the major drawbacks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a solid-state fault isolation device is feasible for use in power electronics based medium voltage distribution systems.
a SSFID is not a single device, but an ensemble of devices that are selected to meet the specific requirements of the application.
a new class of SSFID devices is needed for power electronics based distribution networks.
